intro: These are the rules Claude follows before putting any community place, photo or correction into the app. Jo-Anne wrote them. If any rule fails or Claude is unsure, nothing is published: the item is declined, or it waits under Needs your decision.

rules.text: No people in any photo. Portraits, crowds, children and anyone whose face could be recognised are held back, whether the photo is new or old.
Nothing explicit, violent, gory or hateful in any photo. When in doubt, hold it back. A photo that might show a child being harmed is deleted, never described, and Jo-Anne is told right away.
No private details visible: licence plates, house numbers on private homes, documents, screens, name tags or anything with personal information.
Every photo clearly shows the named place. Old and recent photos are labelled honestly and are never presented as a pair when they are not.

Rights: Wikimedia Commons photos need a free licence, Library of Congress photos need "No known restrictions", uploads need the contributor's CC BY-SA 4.0 promise. Code checks the licence on record is one of those. Claude holds back anything with a watermark, a stock-photo look or a scan from a book.
Up to 5 photos per place, and each must show something a little different (angle, detail, season, old versus recent). Code enforces the limit of 5. Claude holds back near-duplicates.
The place is historic, and open to the public or plainly visible from public ground. Private homes, places closed to visitors and unsafe places are declined.

Not a duplicate. The same name in the same town, the same name as an official stop, or a spot within 150 m of an existing official or community stop counts as a duplicate. Code checks all three. Only Jo-Anne can allow an exception.
The location comes from an official page or two sources that agree, with a radius of 50 to 1000 m. Code checks the numbers. Claude cross-checks the source.
The access note is specific (at least 40 characters): what can be seen from public ground, and to check hours before going.
Every new place is added to Explore History only. Claude never makes a mission. Only Jo-Anne promotes a place to a mission.
At least 2 https sources that Claude actually read in that run. Every fact is tied to the source that supports it, and every source supports a fact. Nothing comes from memory.
Where sources disagree, the card says so. Nothing is invented. The contributor's note is a pointer, not a source. A correction is applied only if a source Claude read supports it.
No private person's name, phone number, email or home address in the text. Code scans for emails, phone numbers and web links. Claude checks the rest. Historic figures named in sources are fine.
Hard history is told briefly and factually with a Sensitive history note. No graphic detail.
Factual and a little warm. No slang, no advertising, no promotion of a business. Code checks there are no web links in the text. Claude checks the tone.
A credit nickname is 1 to 30 plain characters, with no links or contact details, and not a full real name. Code checks length and characters. Claude checks the rest.
At most 5 new places are added in one day. The rest wait for the next run.
When Claude is unsure about anything above, it does not approve. The item goes to Needs your decision on this page and waits for Jo-Anne.
